svg.text: SHEET 06 · ONE JOURNEY, NINE BEATS · VERSION 02
Home to the stadium at walking pace. The resident always walks left to right; every panel’s exit is the next panel’s entrance. Places are the protagonists — buildings frame, they never anchor.
ground-level camera (34/6.5) · locked language throughout · no people, life implied
the paper on the step, the bin at the kerb — Tuesday is already written
houses keep time; trees carry the beat; nothing asks for attention
the road steps back, the forecourt opens — you smell it before you see it
the widest, emptiest moment of the walk — buildings retreat to the edges
parapet at leaning height; the one stop that needs no excuse
compression after the green — awnings, signs, and both accents at once
the second opening, social this time — stalls, notices, the pillar box
hedges narrow, houses fall away, scarves multiply — you hear it first
an honest brick wall, two turnstiles, lights overhead — no spectacle needed
quiet → rhythm → warmth → breath → pause → colour → gathering → anticipation → arrival — compression before every release, and never two open beats in a row.
SHEET 05 GAVE IT MEMORY · SHEET 06 GIVES IT PACE
the player learns the town by walking it — nobody reads a map of home

WHY IT HOLDS — enclosure and openness alternate on a 30–40 second cycle: street → bakery square (open) → oak (widest) → bridge (narrow) → high street (loudest) → market (social) → lane (quiet) → ground (release). The senses arrive before their sources — smell before the bakery, sound before the ground.

WEAK TRANSITIONS, NAMED — 5→6 (bridge to high street) turns without a hinge: insert the CORNER WALL (PL-03) as the pivot. 3→4 (bakery to oak) is abrupt: let the NOTICE BOARD (PL-09) herald the green at the square’s exit. Both are one-prop fixes, already in the vocabulary.

CANONICAL WALK, RECOMMENDED — DOOR · QUIET STREET · BAKERY SQUARE · OAK · BRIDGE · HIGH STREET · MARKET · LANE · GROUND, with the two hinges above. Every ERA town keeps these nine beats and this order; the places themselves may differ town to town — the rhythm is the canon.
